newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil tip upwards, NYMEX heat leads.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil tip upwards, NYMEX heat leads.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil and gas oil made gains in the afternoon in a market led higher by NYMEX heating oil, brokers said.

Buy stops were triggered on the prompt June Brent contract bringing the contract up to an intra-day high of $18.19 a barrel, but the impetus failed to continue and the contract dropped back to last trade up 16 cents at $18.13 a barrel by 1554 GMT.

"There was good volume buying at the stops but there is no conscious effort to push it (June Brent) up to $18.30 things are easing off. Colder weather in Europe and the U.S. is helping this market," one London-based broker said.
Gas oil kept pace with the crude gains and was last done up $1.50 a tonne at $167, some 75 cents off the day's high.
June heating oil on the NYMEX led the complex up and traded last up one cent a gallon at 54.05 cents, just off the day's high of 54.10 cents.
Expectations of tightening heating oil supplies in the U.S. triggered the afternoon's upward leap, U.S. analysts said.

The American Petroleum Institute is expected to report on weekly U.S. oil statistics after the markets close on Tuesday. Preliminary expectations from analysts and traders are for U.S. distillate stocks to be unchanged to down a million barrels from last week. Distillate stocks are being drained by unseasonably cold weather in the key heating oil market of the U.S. Northeast.
